MPs Warn Digital Landline Switchover Risks Emergency Connectivity in Remote UK Areas

Concerns Over Infrastructure Resilience

UK MPs have raised urgent alarms regarding the ongoing transition from traditional copper-wire landlines to internet-based digital services. The shift, scheduled for completion by January, removes the analogue network's ability to operate during power cuts—a feature relied upon by remote communities during extreme weather.

Potential Impact on Vulnerable Residents

Lawmakers representing regions like the Western Isles and Lake District argue that reliance on fibre-optic routers and temporary battery backups is inadequate for isolated households. In severe storms, both internet connectivity and local mobile masts may fail, potentially leaving residents unable to call for emergency assistance. Security Minister Dan Jarvis acknowledged these concerns, promising further review at an upcoming government resilience summit. Residents are encouraged to contact their providers regarding mandatory battery backup units for telecare users. Further guidance is available at https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x29g1nlr51o.
